Story file and mapping: - docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md exists and matches the assessed content (same requirements and acceptance criteria as referenced in prior assessment). - Implementation helpers and rules carry explicit traceability to this story: - src/rules/helpers/valid-implements-utils.ts JSDoc: - @story docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md - @req REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT - src/rules/helpers/valid-req-reference-helpers.ts header: - @supports docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md REQ-SUPPORTS-VALIDATE REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT REQ-SCOPED-IDS - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts header ties REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT to this story.
Core functionality & format validation (REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION, Core Functionality AC): - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - Detects @supports lines: const isImplements = /@supports\b/.test(normalized); - For @supports lines, strips the tag and calls validateImplementsAnnotation(context, comment, implementsValue, options). - Meta.docs and messages describe handling of @story, @req, and @supports. - src/rules/helpers/valid-implements-utils.ts: - MIN_IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS = 2 enforces minimal "storyPath + at least one REQ". - parseImplementsTokens() trims and splits the raw value, reports via: - reportMissingImplementsValue(...) when no value. - reportMissingImplementsReqIds(...) when only storyPath. - validateImplementsTokens() checks storyPath against options.storyPattern and each reqId against options.reqPattern, reporting via: - reportInvalidImplementsStoryPath(...). - reportInvalidImplementsReqId(...), which delegates to buildReqErrorMessage. - validateImplementsAnnotationHelper(...) wires parsing and validation for @supports. - Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts (all passing in Jest run) explicitly cover: - Valid @supports examples: - "[REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE] valid single @supports with one story and one requirement (default patterns)" with code: /** @supports docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE */ - "[REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE] valid multiple @supports lines with different stories and requirements". - "[REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT] valid mixed @story/@req/@supports usage in same block comment". - Invalid @supports formats (ensuring REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE and REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION): - "[REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE] @supports with no value is invalid" → messageId invalidImplementsFormat with clear details. - "[REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE] @supports with only story path and no requirement IDs is invalid". - "[REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION] @supports with invalid story path format". - "[REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION] @supports with invalid requirement ID format". - "[REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION] @supports with multiple requirement IDs where one is invalid".
Requirement validation, scoping & error context (REQ-SUPPORTS-VALIDATE, REQ-SCOPED-IDS, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, Validation AC, Requirement Scoping AC): - src/rules/helpers/valid-req-reference-helpers.ts: - parseImplementsLine(line): detects "@supports ...", returns { storyPath, reqIds }. - validateImplementsLine(...): - Uses validateAndResolveStoryPath(...) and loadAndCacheRequirements(resolvedStoryPath, reqCache) to read requirements from the referenced story file. - For each reqId, calls checkRequirementExists({ comment, context, reqId, storyPath, reqSet }), which reports: context.report({ messageId: 'reqMissing', data: { reqId, storyPath } }) on missing IDs. - Requirements are stored per storyPath in the cache, so IDs are scoped per story file by design. - src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts: - meta.messages.reqMissing = "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" (explicit story-path error context). - createValidReqReferenceProgramVisitor wires the helper logic into the ESLint rule. - Tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts: - Valid @supports multi-story cases (explicitly referencing this story): - "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] single supports line with multiple requirements in multi-story fixture (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)" with code: // @supports tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md REQ-SHARED-ID REQ-ONLY-A - "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] multi-story supports with shared requirement IDs (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)" using both story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md. * Fixtures: - tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md defines REQ-SHARED-ID and REQ-ONLY-A. - tests/fixtures/story_multi_b.md defines REQ-SHARED-ID and REQ-ONLY-B. * This verifies requirement ID reuse across story files (REQ-SCOPED-IDS). - Invalid @supports multi-story cases: - "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] missing supports requirement in multi-story fixture (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)" with code: // @supports tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md REQ-NOT-IN-A expecting messageId 'reqMissing' with data { reqId: 'REQ-NOT-IN-A', storyPath: 'tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md' } → validates error context and scoping. - "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] disallow path traversal in supports story path (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)" with code: // @supports ../tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md REQ-SHARED-ID expecting messageId 'invalidPath' with the bad storyPath → validates path security for @supports.
Rules accept @supports as satisfying story/requirement rules & mixed usage (REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-SUPPORTS, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT, Backward Compatibility AC, Mixed Usage AC): - Story presence (require-story-annotation): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts and related helpers treat @supports as an acceptable marker when searching for story annotations near functions; this is verified indirectly by tests in tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts: - Valid cases include branches annotated only with @supports: * "[REQ-SUPPORTS-ALTERNATIVE] if-statement with only @supports annotation is treated as fully annotated". * "[REQ-SUPPORTS-ALTERNATIVE] try/catch where both branches are annotated only with @supports". * "[REQ-SUPPORTS-ALTERNATIVE] else-if branch with @supports inside the block body". - Requirement presence (require-req-annotation): - src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts: - commentContainsReq, linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq all treat lines containing either @req or @supports as satisfying requirement presence. - hasReqAnnotation(...) ultimately returns true when either @req or @supports is found near the node. - Tests in tests/utils/req-annotation-detection.test.ts explicitly confirm this: - "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQ-DETECTION] treats @supports in comments as satisfying requirement". - Other tests show @supports in leading comments and ancestor comments are accepted. - Mixed usage and backward compatibility: - Legacy @story/@req handling in valid-annotation-format remains intact (extensive tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts for single- and multi-line @story and @req, configurable patterns, etc.). - Mixed usage test: - "[REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT] valid mixed @story/@req/@supports usage in same block comment" shows all three styles coexisting and passing validation. - @story + @req validation (no @supports) is still verified by many tests in valid-req-reference.test.ts and valid-annotation-format.test.ts, ensuring REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT.
Error messages & inclusion of story context (REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, Error Messages AC): - valid-annotation-format @supports errors: - src/rules/helpers/valid-implements-utils.ts report* functions construct detailed human-readable messages used via meta.messages.invalidImplementsFormat and invalidReqFormat in src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts. - Tests verify messageId and details text for missing values, missing req IDs, invalid story paths, and invalid req IDs. - Requirement existence errors: - src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts meta.messages.reqMissing = "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'". - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts invalid cases (including @supports ones) assert both reqId and storyPath in data, satisfying REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT and the acceptance criterion about indicating which story was checked.
Documentation & migration guidance (Documentation AC): - user-docs/migration-guide.md contains a dedicated section "3.1 Multi-story `@supports` annotations" which: - Shows concrete @supports examples, including one with this story path: - * @supports docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE REQ-IMPLEMENTS-VALIDATE - Explains that @story/@req remain supported and that @supports is for genuine multi-story integration cases. - Documents the optional migration rule traceability/prefer-supports-annotation and how it rewrites eligible @story + @req blocks to @supports. - Describes mixed usage scenarios and gradual migration, matching the story’s documentation and migration-strategy notes. - README.md and user-docs materials describe @supports semantics and the migration aid rule, aligning with ADR 011’s decision captured in the story.
Quality & tests (Quality Standards AC, Tests in Definition of Done): - Rules involved (valid-annotation-format, valid-req-reference, helpers, reqAnnotationDetection) follow ESLint best practices: - Each rule exports meta (docs, messages, schema) and create; tests use RuleTester with comprehensive valid/invalid cases. - Multi-story @supports behavior is factored into small helpers (valid-implements-utils, valid-req-reference-helpers, reqAnnotationDetection) with their own tests. - Direct tests tied to this story: - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts header purposely references docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md and REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE / REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION / REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT. - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts gives multi-story @supports cases explicitly annotated in names as "see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT". - Full test execution: - Command run: npm test -- --verbose - Jest output shows all suites passing, including: - "Valid Annotation Format Rule (Story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION)" with all @supports-related tests passing (REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT scenarios). - "Valid Req Reference Rule (Story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION)" with the multi-story @supports tests linked to 010.2 passing for both valid and invalid cases. - Summary (from latest run): Test Suites: 1 skipped, 48 passed (48/49 total); Tests: 2 skipped, 369 passed (371 total); no failures related to this story or @supports.
Backward-compat and ADR alignment: - The multi-story behavior uses @supports as the canonical tag for combined story+requirement lines, as required by this story (no code path uses @implements for multi-story parsing). - Historical/@implements naming appears only in internal identifiers and in a separate migration rule (prefer-implements-annotation as an alias for prefer-supports-annotation), but the parsing and validation for multi-story annotations themselves are all keyed on @supports, consistent with the ADR 011 alignment note in the story.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria in 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT are satisfied: - @supports annotations are parsed and format-validated independently of @story/@req. - Every @supports requirement is validated against its referenced story file, with errors clearly indicating the specific story path and requirement ID. - Backward compatibility with existing @story/@req annotations is preserved, and mixed usage (including combining @story, @req, and @supports in the same comment/file) is fully supported and tested. - Requirement IDs are scoped per story file through a per-path requirements cache. - Implementation follows ESLint rule best practices and is thoroughly covered by targeted RuleTester suites and integration tests. - Documentation in user-docs/migration-guide.md and related docs clearly explains @supports usage, semantics, and migration from legacy annotations. The story file hasn’t changed in a way that invalidates prior evidence, and a fresh full Jest run confirms all relevant tests still pass, so the story is fully implemented.
